newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-STEWART HITS RECORD 173 FOR ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STEWART HITS RECORD 173 FOR ENGLAND.

text.p: A record knock by wicketkeeper Alec Stewart (173) and a return to form by skipper Mike Atherton (83) ensured England's hopes were kept alive in their first test match against New Zealand on Sunday.
By the close of the third day the test was evenly balanced, with England at 366 for six in reply to New Zealand's first innings total of 390.
However, the newly-laid Eden Park strip -- being used for the first time in this test -- has favoured the batsmen so far.
With the pitch offering only slow turn for the spinners and the odd low bounce, Stewart, Atherton and left-hander Graham Thorpe (57 not out) cashed in.
Stewart started this morning on 67 and hardly put a foot wrong on his way to his 173 -- a record for an England test wicketkeeper. He drove impressively and was quick to punish anything short.

He got to his 10th test hundred -- and his fourth against New Zealand -- with a sharp single to mid on shortly before lunch. The century came off 161 balls, with 14 fours and a six, and with Atherton had taken England to 193 for one at lunch.
Atherton was patient, producing the occasional flowing drive and clipped stroke through mid wicket as he found the form which has eluded him so far on the tours of Zimbabwe and New Zealand.
But Atherton's march towards an 11th test hundred ended in unusual fashion, 17 runs short.
He slammed a ball from Dipak Patel back down the onside of the pitch. Justin Vaughan, fielding at a shortish mid on position, palmed the ball up and Patel grabbed the rebound.
Stewart cruised past 150 and by tea had reached 165. But with his sights on a first test double century, Stewart fell to a smart, low return catch taken by fast-medium bowler Simon Doull.
New Zealand had a glimmer of hope in the final hour.

John Crawley had looked in good touch getting to 14 when he drove a ball to mid on and set off for a comfortable run. Thorpe didn't move as Doull sprawled to his left, gathered the ball and threw it back to wicketkeeper Lee Germon with both batsmen at the non-striker's end.
Vaughan then had Craig White leg before wicket next ball and 339 for four had become 339 for six.
With two days left to play, it is difficult to imagine either side getting a result, but New Zealand captain Germon was optimistic.

"If we can bowl them out in the first session tomorrow, set a target on the last day, it's definitely winnable. It's going to get progressively lower and be harder to score runs on the last day," he said.
